```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
options(digits = 5, width = 95)
```

Most chamber users (unsaturated surfaces) never meet ebullition and never
need this vignette: the core path of `fluxqc`
(`goFlux -> best.flux -> flag_detection -> qc_screens`, wrapped by
`process_fluxes()`) does not call any of the code below. Over water,
saturated peat or flooded vegetation, bubbles add abrupt step-ups to the
smooth diffusive rise, and one linear or Hutchinson-Mosier fit through both
components gives a number that is neither.

**Since goFlux 0.3.0 this is goFlux's job.** Camille Minaudo added
`goAquaFlux()` (with the internal `find.bubbles()` and `flux.plot.aqua()`):
bubbling events are detected per closure from the rolling dispersion of the
concentration series with an adaptive median + k x MAD threshold, each
event's step magnitude is estimated by a local step regression that separates
the step from the diffusive trend and from the transient peak and
re-equilibration that follow a bubble (goFlux 0.4.0), the diffusive flux is
fitted with goFlux's own model selection on the bubble-free part of the
trace, and the ebullitive flux comes from the summed step magnitudes.
`fluxqc` therefore no longer implements its own detector: the add-on is a
thin adapter, `detect_ebullition()`, that forwards a click.peak2-style table
to `goAquaFlux()` and appends the result to the flux table when
`process_fluxes(ebullition = "flag" | "split")` is used. Despite its name,
`goAquaFlux()` needs only `Vtot`, `Area`, `Pcham`, `Tcham` (and `Etime`,
`flag`), so it applies to any bubbling surface.

## A real closure with a bubble burst

`ebullition_floating` in `fluxqc_examples()` is a real 276 s floating-chamber
closure on open water at a ghost-forest mangrove site of the NASA BlueFlux
campaign (ABB/LGR GLA131). Geometry: Area 324.3 cm2, Vtot 4.318 L, Tcham
28.7 C, Pcham 101.325 kPa. CH4 rises diffusively from the first sample while
CO2 rises cleanly from t = 0 (the chamber was already sealed); at 42-46 s the
CH4 jumps by about 675 ppb over five consecutive samples (one burst; the
campaign's own single-sample threshold counted it as "5 jumps"), then resumes
a steady rise. We put it next to the clean closure `emission_stem_semirigid`.

```{r make}
library(fluxqc)
ex <- fluxqc_examples(c("ebullition_floating", "emission_stem_semirigid"))
both <- ex$data
ex$aux[, c("UniqueID", "obs.length", "Area", "Vtot", "Tcham", "analyzer")]
e <- both[both$UniqueID == "ebullition_floating", ]
```

## Detection and partition with goAquaFlux

```{r detect, fig.height = 5}
invisible(capture.output(eb <- suppressWarnings(detect_ebullition(both, "CH4dry_ppb"))))
eb$summary
eb$events[, c("UniqueID", "start", "end", "magnitude", "SE", "slope", "n_used", "overshoot")]
ev <- eb$events
op <- par(mfrow = c(2, 1), mar = c(4, 4.5, 2.5, 1))
plot(e$Etime, e$CH4dry_ppb, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, type = "b", xlab = "seconds since window start",
     ylab = "CH4 (ppb)", main = "goAquaFlux: event window (red) and settled step magnitude")
rect(ev$start, min(e$CH4dry_ppb), ev$end, max(e$CH4dry_ppb), col = rgb(1, 0, 0, 0.12), border = NA)
abline(v = c(ev$start, ev$end), col = "red", lty = 2)
text(ev$end, max(e$CH4dry_ppb), sprintf("step: +%.0f ppb (SE %.1f)", ev$magnitude, ev$SE), pos = 4, col = "red", cex = 0.8)
plot(e$Etime, e$CO2dry_ppm, pch = 16, cex = 0.5, type = "b", xlab = "seconds since window start",
     ylab = "CO2 (ppm)", main = "CO2 rises from t = 0: the chamber was sealed before the burst")
abline(v = c(ev$start, ev$end), col = "red", lty = 2)
par(op)
```

`goAquaFlux()` finds the one event (high-dispersion window `r ev$start`-`r ev$end`
s) and estimates a settled step of `r round(ev$magnitude)` ppb. It reports an
ebullitive flux, but `flux_diffusive` and `flux_total` are `NA` for this
closure: goAquaFlux fits the diffusive term on the observations *before the
first bubble*, and here the burst comes after only ~23 s, too few points.
That is a property of the closure (an early burst), not of the method; for
the clean closure the partition returns the whole-trace flux with zero
ebullition. `goFlux::flux.plot.aqua()` draws goFlux's own diagnostic plot for
such results.

## Through `process_fluxes()`

The add-on is an option of the pipeline, not a separate path. `"flag"` keeps
the whole-trace `best.flux` and records the events; `"split"` additionally
appends goFlux's `flux_diffusive`, `flux_ebullitive`, `flux_total` (with SEs),
`n_obs_diffusive`, `first_bubble_time` and `ebullition_method = "goAquaFlux"`.
goFlux's own columns (`best.flux`, `MDF`, ...) are never modified.
Per-closure control comes from `ebullition_ids` or a logical `ebullition`
column in the auxfile, so the closures known to bubble can be partitioned
while the rest of the same call run the core path.

```{r process}
aux <- data.frame(UniqueID = c("emission_stem_semirigid", "ebullition_floating"), ebullition = c(FALSE, TRUE))
invisible(capture.output(       # goFlux's progress bar is captured
  res <- suppressWarnings(process_fluxes(both, aux = aux, gastype = "CH4dry_ppb",
                       qc = list(c0 = TRUE, convex = TRUE),
                       ebullition = "split"))))
res
res$fluxes[, c("UniqueID", "ebullition_handling", "best.flux", "flux_diffusive", "flux_ebullitive",
               "flux_total", "n_ebullition_events", "first_bubble_time", "MDF_emp", "det_class_emp")]
res$events[, c("UniqueID", "start", "end", "magnitude", "SE")]
```

`write_outputs(res, dir)` then adds `ebullition_events.csv` (goFlux's bubble
table) next to `fluxes.csv` and `settings.json`.

## How other tools handle ebullition

Checked from the sources or manuals named; "not verified" marks claims that
could not be checked.

| tool | ebullition / piecewise handling | verified from |
|---|---|---|
| goFlux >= 0.3.0 (Minaudo) | `goAquaFlux()`: rolling-dispersion detection with adaptive MAD threshold, local step regression with re-equilibration model (0.4.0), diffusion on the pre-bubble window, ebullition from summed steps; `flux.plot.aqua()` | 0.4.0 source (`find.bubbles.R`, `goAquaFlux*.R`) |
| Hoffmann et al. 2017 (AMT 10:109-118), R script on Zenodo record 53168 | quartile fences `Q1 - 0.25 IQR`, `Q3 + 0.25 IQR` on the point-to-point changes; a moving-window linear fit is accepted only when all its changes lie inside the fences | script lines 365-366, 457-458 |
| `fluxCH4` (github.com/mthayne527/fluxCH4; standalone scripts) | GAM per id, otherwise GBMs via `dismo::gbm.step`; smoothed residuals, dynamic threshold and a concentration-difference quantile test; flagged points grouped into sequences | README |
| So et al. 2024 (JGR-B, doi:10.1029/2024JG008035) | running variance above a user cutoff defines event periods | published description; code not verified |
| CRAN `flux` 0.3-0.1 (archived 2026-04-15) | `flux.odae()` excludes outlying points to find stable linear conditions; nothing is quantified as ebullition | `flux.Rd` |
| `gasfluxes` 0.7-2, `HMR` 1.0.5, `fluxfinder` 1.2.2 | no ebullition or piecewise handling mentioned | CRAN manuals |
| `RespChamberProc` (GitHub) | `changepoint`/`segmented` for the initial lag, not ebullition | `R/fluxEstimates.R` |
| `FluxCalR` | no ebullition mention in its README; source not inspected | README |

## Provenance and citation etiquette

`fluxqc`'s add-on contains no detection code of its own: all detection and
partition is `goFlux::goAquaFlux()`, written by Camille Minaudo for goFlux
0.3.0-0.4.0. The earlier fluxqc implementations (a Hoffmann-style IQR fence
filter, a fixed threshold and a running-variance method, none of which copied
code from the Hoffmann Zenodo script or fluxCH4) were removed as duplicates.
If you publish results obtained with the add-on, cite goFlux (Rheault,
Christiansen & Larsen 2024, JOSS 9(96), 6393, doi:10.21105/joss.06393) and
its aquatic partition (goFlux >= 0.3.0, C. Minaudo; see the goFlux changelog
and package citation) alongside `citation("fluxqc")`.

## Limitations

Inherited from `goAquaFlux()`: the diffusive term needs enough bubble-free
observations before the first event; analyzer artefacts (pressure transients,
breaths on an inlet, valve switches) can look like bubbles; and the
ebullitive rate assumes the bubbles caught in a 5-10 min closure represent
the sampling period, which for episodic ebullition is rarely true. Review
`events` against the traces (and `flux.plot.aqua()`) before reporting.
